title: Format revision: id_matches_file should derive id from parent dir for spec.md files (single-tree spec authoring)
description:
PROBLEM: linter.id_matches_file requires frontmatter id to equal the filename stem, forcing every spec.md (openspec layout) to carry id: spec. Combined with total_refs self-containment for dual-format files, this structurally locks a two-tree architecture: a real-id corpus (specs/) for the typed graph + a deployed dual-format openspec/specs/ tree produced by per-repo hand-rolled transforms (tambor deploy_specs.py + regen gate; specodelic's own verbatim archive-companion deploys have drifted - compile.md, packs.md statements diverge from corpus). New users inherit the distinction and must learn two vocabularies.

PROPOSED REVISION (one rule): for files named spec.md, derive the expected id from the PARENT DIRECTORY name (openspec/specs/ge-cli/spec.md -> ge.cli; - maps to ., _ literal). Everything else already verified compatible with a single tree (openspec/ layout as the only spec home): openspec validate --strict passes 19/19 on four-layer dual-format content given ## Purpose + SHALL in mirror requirement (pilot, 2026-10-08); spk lint total_refs resolves cross-file links across the lint set (prose links unaffected); ah/espectacular reads paths.specs from config. Empirical wall test: dropping a real-id corpus file as openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md yields exactly one finding - id_matches_file.

REVISED RULE SEMANTICS: real-id four-layer files with hand-maintained ## Requirements mirror become the authoring format everywhere; ## Purpose promoted from prose under H1; mirror requirement text must contain SHALL/MUST (openspec strict keyword check); id: spec + self-containment + per-repo deploy transforms + regen gates all retire.

ROLLOUT AFTER REVISION: (1) specodelic new default target -> openspec/specs/<id>/spec.md so new users cannot produce the two-tree distinction; (2) update SPECODELIC managed block (specodelic init) + guide docs; (3) one-time migration per repo: move corpus file -> openspec/specs/<dir>/spec.md + Purpose + mirror (script validated on gently, 12/12), delete specs/, tools/deploy_specs.py, drift gates; (4) tambor: re-key espectacular contracts from [[spec.*]] to real-id anchors (specodelic rename is atomic for this); (5) dogfood: specodelic's own specs/ corpus migrates last; compile.md/packs.md divergence resolved by taking corpus as truth; (6) archive-companion's verbatim-deploy write path retired or redefined.

GOVERNANCE: format revision bump (Revision 17 -> 18) per specs/specodelic.md; this repo's own openspec change workflow. Pilot session notes: gently corpus, 12 files, transform script validated idempotent.

title: p1 errors: failures ride success-shaped envelopes — refuted claim exits 0 (F1)
description:
Found by the 2026-10-08 external evaluation reports (Claude Sonnet 5.5 report, finding F1); re-verified on current tree at bd6585b.

**Symptom** (all reproduced on the quick-start spec from specs/USAGE.md §1):
- `spk model-check` with a **refuted** kernel claim: exit **0**, JSON `ok:true`, `outcome: counterexample_found`. The sharpest case.
- `compile` with a kernel-grammar failure: exit 1 but `ok:true` / `envelope_kind: ok`, `files_failed: 1`.
- `model-check` stale, `verify` blocked, `orchestrate` verify-stage failure: same shape — non-zero exit riding a success envelope.

**Expected** (specs/errors.md rows `envelope_error_kind`, `exit_code_mapping`, `remediation_hint_present`): a failure must never ride a success-shaped envelope; exit 1 means findings-or-failure and `ok` must reflect it.

**Impact**: CI/scripts gating on `.ok` (the documented success signal) pass failing runs. `CHANGELOG.md` #116 already declares `counterexample_found` a failing aggregate outcome.

**Repro**:
```
spk compile order-cancel.md
# change kernel row to a refutable claim, then:
spk model-check order-cancel.md; echo $?   # 0, outcome counterexample_found
```

**Open question for the fix**: decide whether `ok` means "tool ran" (reconcile specs/errors.md) or "run succeeded" (fix exit/envelope emission). Also fold in F7 documentation: verify's scope digest binds inputs, not result statuses — forged check.json statuses yield model gate `state: clean`; document or bind.

Source: ~/Downloads/cv/specodelic-unreleased-evaluation.md §4 F1, F7.
acceptance_criteria: Must: every case in the body's symptom table exits per the specs/errors.md mapping — failures carry ok:false / envelope_kind:error (or a findings-shaped envelope the spec sanctions) and a refuted kernel claim exits 1. Meter: the body's F1 repro sequence, re-run at base_commit, prints exit 1 plus a non-success envelope for each listed case; any case still printing exit 0 with ok:true = not done.
notes: ANTI-GOALS: do not weaken findings emission or the envelope warnings/hints fields; do not make batch commands exit 0 to hide partial failure; exit codes may only move toward the specs/errors.md mapping, never away from it.
close_reason: Fixed: failures ride error-kind envelopes (ok:false) and a refuted kernel claim exits 1 — meter re-verified, just ci green, commit c81d9af

title: corpus artifacts: check reports re-keyed without re-run — fabricated provenance; add corpus-wide model-check/verify CI gate
description:
Reproduced 2026-10-03: the corpus artifacts committed in 169ba20 ("regenerate compiled corpus — modules carry the Revision 15 manifest line, check reports re-keyed to the new artifact hashes") carry check reports whose SHA fields were EDITED to match the new modules, while outcome/invariants fields were NOT refreshed by an actual run.

Evidence: specodelic/compile.check.json reports outcome=exploration_only, invariants_checked=[] and its artifact_sha256 matches the committed specodelic/compile.tla — but that .tla contains 5 prose "INVARIANT" entries (see specodelic-sd1), and running the CURRENT binary against it fails the scratch run. A run that had actually executed would have reported the failure (MUST: a scratch failure is labeled, never silent). So the committed report describes a check that did not happen against the module version it claims to hash — exactly the fabricated-provenance shape specodelic-8nt was filed to prevent.

Also: `just ci` is green despite model-check failing 2/22 and verify uncompilable on 7/22 — no CI stage runs model-check/verify over the corpus, so pipeline regressions ship invisible.

GREEN:
1. CI gate: add a corpus-wide `spk model-check specs` + `spk verify specs` stage to just ci (or at minimum model-check) once sd1/8aq land — the pipeline must be exercised on the corpus it ships with.
2. Regenerate specodelic/ artifacts honestly (re-run, never re-key): check.json outcome/invariants/sha must all come from one actual run.
3. Anti-goal: no hand-edited artifact fields; if regeneration is impractical for a commit, don't commit refreshed hashes — stale-but-honest beats fresh-but-fabricated.
acceptance_criteria: Must: (1) a CI stage (justfile recipe wired into `just ci`) runs `spk model-check specs` and fails the gate on any non-clean outcome it cannot honestly produce; (2) specodelic/*.check.json regenerated by an actual run — outcome, invariants_checked, and artifact_sha256 all from one invocation; (3) zero hand-edited artifact fields (git history of the regen commit shows a single regen). Meter: just ci (new stage included); git log -p -- specodelic/ shows re-run provenance. Anti-goals: never commit re-keyed hashes again — stale-but-honest beats fresh-but-fabricated; no weakening of the MUST-labeled-failure rule from specodelic-8nt.
close_reason: e6287ed: model-check-specs recipe wired into just ci (cargo run, fails on non-clean outcome); artifact honesty re-verified — regen is byte-identical no-op vs HEAD, zero hand-edited fields; verify gate deferred (18/18 todo_predicate! stubs fail honestly by design until rust: fragment migration)

title: model-check: **rust:** marker mentions in defining rows trip fragment extraction — scratch run fails 2/22 corpus files
description:
Reproduced 2026-10-03 (corpus-wide run): `spk model-check specs` hard-fails 2 of 22 files — specs/compile.md and specs/model_check.md — with "the executable-invariant scratch run failed (exit status: 101)".

Root cause: the **rust:** marker detector trips on MENTIONS, not opt-ins. The corpus rows that DEFINE the marker (compile.md's predicate_fragment_opt_in / invariant_fragment_opt_in / fragment_law_rejected / fragment_guard_rejected / properties_to_proptest; model_check.md's executable_invariants_execute) contain the literal text `**rust:**` inside backtick code spans in their own expr cells. The extractor treats the prose after the mention as the "fragment" — e.g. compile.tla line 8-11 carries `INVARIANT properties_to_proptest **rust:** fragment when the row opts in...` — prose, not Rust. The scratch crate then fails to compile it (21 errors for compile, unbalanced delimiter for model_check).

This is the exact bootstrapping-bug shape specodelic.md's Notes warn about: the tool's own description of the mechanism breaks the mechanism.

Evidence: TLA manifest lines above; committed specodelic/compile.tla has 5 bogus INVARIANT entries; scratch errors name prose ("fragment when the row's kind is invariant — the fragment becomes an executable invariant...").

RED: test asserting a constraint expr that merely MENTIONS `**rust:**` inside a code span produces NO executable invariant (and ideally an advisory), while a real opt-in (marker followed by Rust outside code spans) still extracts.

GREEN (two-sided):
1. impl: marker detection must ignore `**rust:**` inside code spans (backticks); the opt-in is the marker OUTSIDE code spans. Consider whether fragment_hygiene should label an ambiguous cell instead of silently mis-extracting.
2. spec: sharpen predicate_fragment_opt_in/invariant_fragment_opt_in wording — a mention inside a code span is not an opt-in (Revision 15 note or Revision 16).

Then regenerate the corpus honestly (see the provenance ticket) — model-check specs must go 22/22.
acceptance_criteria: Must: (1) a RED tests/cli.rs fixture whose constraint expr merely mentions `**rust:**` inside a backtick code span produces NO executable invariant (compile.tla carries no INVARIANT line for it); (2) a real opt-in (marker outside code spans, Rust after it) still extracts verbatim; (3) `spk model-check specs` reports 22 checked, 0 failed. Meter: cargo test --test cli (red first at base_commit); ./target/debug/specodelic model-check specs == 22/22; just ci green. Anti-goals: do not weaken the four fragment-rejection rows (law/guard/non-invariant/multi-marker/empty); no mini-language introduced; no change to law-case splitting.
notes: Co-modification note (issue-review PRE-002-adjacent): this ticket and specodelic-8aq both touch src/compile.rs (fragment extraction vs property emission). They are parallelizable; whoever lands second must re-anchor base_commit and rebase. No new files — no file-header criterion needed.
close_reason: eef9015: fragment-position rule (cell-start or span-opening); mentions ignored; compile.md rows sharpened, verify.md reworded; model-check specs 20/20 scratch-clean

title: lint: implement tiered single_root_reachable (own-file primary linkage) — spec-vs-tool drift (Ro5 CORR-001)
description:
Rule-of-5 corpus review (2026-10-01) CORR-001 (HIGH): the shipped single_root_reachable drifted from its spec — three-way divergence.

SPEC (authority): specs/specodelic.md Revision 10 + specs/linter-graph_shape.md:19 (expr) and its Notes — reachability lands on the file's OWN intent through own-file primary linkage; cross-file typed edges (guard citations of foreign constraints, satisfies, observes) are outbound leaves, never reachability paths; enforcement is TIERED — rows whose only connection is cross-file are advisory-flagged first, hard enforcement flips after corpus reconciliation (specodelic-cxq, now closed, so the flip is due).

SHIPPED: src/lint.rs:678-687 implements undirected connectivity to SOME intent row; its comment cites "checker spec text as written" — a stale reference to the pre-Rev-10 text. The advisory tier exists nowhere in src/. The RULE_TABLE semantics string (src/lint.rs:145) documents the loose reading, so `spk explain lint-rules` actively advertises the superseded semantics.

Impact: the exact "bootstrapping bug" shape specodelic.md's Notes warn about (tool disagrees with its own description; self-lint structurally blind — a weak checker passes the corpus by construction). Rev 10 called the loose reading dangerous: it silently accepts cross-file/wrong-id filing.

SCOPE (TDD, red first):
1. RED: tests/cli.rs fixture — a spec file whose rows connect only through a cross-file typed edge (e.g. a constraint citing a foreign constraint via guard, with no own-file traces_to path) must produce the advisory cross-file-only warning, not pass silently; a row with no path to ANY intent still fails single_root_reachable.
2. GREEN: implement own-file primary-linkage reachability in src/graph.rs/lint.rs; cross-file-only rows ride the warnings channel (advisory, exit 0) per Rev 10's tier; hard failure stays for rows unreachable from any intent. Update RULE_TABLE src/lint.rs:145 to the own-file wording + tier note.
3. Verify: whether the corpus now passes own-file enforcement post-cxq reconciliation (expect yes — the traces_to reconciliation landed); if rows fail, they are genuine Rev 10 anchors to fix in the same ticket.
4. Pinning test: unit test asserting the reachability semantics (own-file, not corpus-wide) so it cannot silently regress again.

Base the semantics rewording on specodelic.md Rev 10's exact language; specodelic.md and linter-graph_shape.md need no changes (they are already correct).
acceptance_criteria: Must: (1) a tests/cli.rs fixture whose rows connect only via a cross-file typed edge produces an advisory cross-file-only warning (exit 0) instead of passing silently; (2) a row with no path to ANY intent still fails single_root_reachable; (3) RULE_TABLE semantics string states the own-file reading; (4) corpus stays green. Meter: cargo test single_root (red-first must fail at base_commit); cargo test --test cli; just ci green; spk lint specs reports 0 issues and the fixture warning rides the warnings channel. Anti-goals: no new Reference Typing rows, no format Revision, do not weaken or remove any existing lint rule, do not hard-fail corpus rows whose only connection is cross-file (that is the advisory tier's job).

title: no_counterexample with zero invariants is a false green — model-check must execute invariants or downgrade the verdict
description:
Reproduced: model-check reports outcome=no_counterexample with invariants_checked:[] (see specodelic/merge.check.json). A clean verdict over an empty invariant set implies verification that did not happen.

RED: test asserts that a report with invariants_checked:[] carries outcome != no_counterexample (e.g. vacuous_clean / not_checked) or fails the stage.

title: Input hardening: lint hangs forever on a FIFO named *.md and reads /dev/zero unbounded (OOM)
description:
Reproduced: mkfifo /tmp/x.md && spk lint /tmp/x.md blocks forever (timed out, exit 124); /dev/zero hits the same unbounded read path and OOM-kills (confirmed mechanism, tested under ulimit). Ingestion uses std::fs::read_to_string with no file-type or size check (src/main.rs:486 and :1110).

RED: tests — (a) lint on a FIFO named *.md returns a labeled error within a timeout, never blocks; (b) lint on an oversized regular file (> cap) returns a labeled error naming the cap.
GREEN: require f.metadata()?.is_file() (or file_type().is_file()) before reading; enforce a size cap (e.g. 2 MiB — corpus files are ~10-50 KB) with a remediation hint naming the offending path. Same treatment for compile/verify/graph ingestion paths that share the discovery code.
Evidence: review round 2, issue 6.
notes: SCOPE ADDITION 2026-09-29 (review round 2, path-to-prod step 4): include codegen identifier sanitizing hardening in this ticket — verify compile's row-id → Rust-identifier sanitization (src/compile.rs law-case fn naming) covers hostile ids (leading digits, unicode, reserved words, extremely long ids) with a RED test per class; the ingestion file-type check and the codegen sanitizer share the 'hostile input' theme and both gate trust in emitted artifacts.

title: Implement specodelic compile: Set^K -> TOML / TLA+ / proptest functor
description:
Per specs/compile.md. Translate a linted-and-covered spec file's Constraints table into a TOML document, its Model section into a TLA+ (or Alloy) module, and its Properties table into proptest! blocks — without dropping or altering any id.

MUST: ids in == ids out for every compiled file (compile_preserves_ids, no_semantic_drift); a Properties row yields a proptest! block that compiles.
METER: `spk compile <file> --json` exits 0 per file; corpus-wide demo requires specodelic-qc8 closed (precondition_satisfied demands linted+covered).
TASK LADDER (keep ticket whole per compile.md's single Compile transition): 1) Constraints→TOML, 2) Model→TLA+, 3) Properties→proptest!.
TOOLCHAIN: toml crate (already a dep); TLA+ emitted as text (checking it is nx7's job); proptest dep to add.
ANTI-GOALS: never parse prose (prose_untouched); never mint, drop, or alter ids; no orchestration logic here (that's 8kk).

title: migrate: mixed-delta (ADDED+MODIFIED) file gets an ADDED-only mirror and immediately fails lint
description:
From the 2026-10-08 Qwen chat report (its one live claim — the rest were stale); re-verified at bd6585b.

**Repro**:
```
printf '## ADDED Requirements\n\n### Requirement: One\none holds\n\n## MODIFIED Requirements\n\n### Requirement: Two\ntwo holds\n' > delta.md
spk migrate delta.md   # exit 0
spk lint delta.md      # exit 1: linter.requirement_drift
```

**Observed**: migrate writes the mirror as a byte-exact copy of the `## ADDED Requirements` body only (src/migrate.rs D6 doc comment); the MODIFIED section is dropped. Since changelog #93, `linter.requirement_drift` compares per requirement across **all** carried delta sections — so the freshly migrated file is guaranteed to fail lint.

**Fix direction** (pick one):
1. Aggregate ADDED + MODIFIED bodies into the mirror (mirrors the per-requirement lint rule), or
2. Refuse mixed deltas labeled ("migrate handles ADDED-only deltas; MODIFIED requires hand-mirroring") and document it.

Option 1 is preferred — silent guaranteed-failure output is worse than either fix.
acceptance_criteria: Must: spk migrate on a mixed ADDED+MODIFIED delta either (a) emits a mirror whose every delta requirement passes spk lint, or (b) refuses labeled with remediation. Meter: the body's repro — after migrate exits 0, spk lint delta.md exits 0; or migrate exits 1 with a labeled message. migrate 0 followed by lint 1 = not done.

title: model-check: stale compile demotes a malformed kernel claim to unchecked — silent clean (F2)
description:
Found by the 2026-10-08 external evaluation (Claude report, finding F2); re-verified at bd6585b.

**Repro**:
```
spk compile order-cancel.md            # succeeds
sed -i 's/resolves(traces_to)/frobnicates(traces_to)/' order-cancel.md
spk model-check order-cancel.md; echo $?   # 0, no_counterexample — malformed claim silently demoted
spk compile order-cancel.md; echo $?       # 1 — labeled kernel_grammar failure
```

**Observed**: the edited cell disappears from the claim list, lands in `unchecked_claim_ids`; run reports clean. `compile` rejects the same input loudly.

**Expected**: the kernel grammar rule says a non-member atom is a labeled failure — "never prose, never silence" (src/kernel.rs ~455-463; `kernel_nonmember_labeled` at specs/compile.md:93).

**Cause**: src/verify.rs `claim_classification` (~line 695) falls through to the `unchecked` branch when `extract_model_ir` has no `guard_kernel` entry for the cell; model-check's staleness check catches edited transitions (exit 1) but not edited constraint cells.

**Mitigations already in place**: `verify` catches the edit via scope digest; `orchestrate` recompiles first. Only standalone `model-check` after a stale compile is affected.

**Fix direction**: extend model-check's staleness check to cover constraint cells (e.g. include structured constraint content in the digest compared pre-check), or fail labeled when a previously-compiled required claim's cell no longer parses.
acceptance_criteria: Must: standalone model-check on a stale compile whose constraint cell breaks the kernel grammar fails labeled — never silently demotes the claim to unchecked and reports clean. Meter: the body's repro — the sed + model-check sequence exits 1 with a labeled kernel-grammar finding; exit 0 with outcome no_counterexample = not done.

title: specodelic-84i
concurrent-session race: transient gate-poison state was committed+pushed by a parallel agent (e7bb19e)
description: During specodelic-c0o gate work (2026-10-03 ~19:36 local), a concurrent pi session (running since Oct 02) committed THIS session's in-flight working-tree edits 13s after its own beads commit: 6 legit contract rebinds PLUS the seeded-violation poison (no-tag-drift.toml → no_such_test_exists_xyz), pushed as e7bb19e with a misleading message ('gate-authored rewrite ... to real test names' — the diff actually INTRODUCES a nonexistent binding). Its pre-commit ran structural-only ah check, so the poison passed the hook; that commit's CI stayed green only because guard-espectacular landed later (7fca7ef). Resolution: 7fca7ef restored correct bindings; a70b88d fixed runner exit-127. Lessons/fix options: (a) seeded-violation drills must run in a worktree or with a concurrency lock; (b) pre-commit should not sweep unrelated staged/unstaged files into a commit attributed to the gate; (c) agents must check git status --short before committing and exclude files they did not author. Verify no repeat: ah check --run-tests green, 135/135.
notes:
Decision 2026-10-04: remediations (a) and (c) filed as child tickets (discovered-from this issue); (b) pre-commit sweep policy is held for deliberate design — it touches the .beads/hooks chain under the AGENTS.md pretender claim-or-chain constraint, needs a design call before ticketing. Parent stays open until (b) is decided or all children close.
Design call on (b) MADE 2026-10-05: adopted policy-first + drill-lock interlock — see openspec/decisions/2026-10-05-precommit-sweep-policy.md. Hook-side change limited to the do8 drill-lock interlock via scripts/guards/ + lefthook.yml (no .beads/hooks edits, no core.hooksPath claims); residual foreign-file sweep risk accepted as policy-mitigated by 2g1; no separate (b) ticket. Parent still closes when do8+2g1 close.
RESOLVED 2026-10-05 — all remediations dispositioned: (a) do8 closed (gate-drill advisory lock: scripts/guards/gate-drill{,-lock}.sh wired via lefthook.yml pre-commit+pre-push + just ci guard-drill-lock; two-session rehearsal on the real hook chain refused a concurrent commit of staged files while a drill was live, hook exit 1; commit 5f4335b). (b) decided — policy-first + drill-lock interlock, no separate ticket (openspec/decisions/2026-10-05-precommit-sweep-policy.md). (c) 2g1 closed (AGENTS.md Commit hygiene standing instruction + .wai/AGENTS.md session-end checklist; foreign-file drill walk-through exercised and documented). No repeat verified: ah check green, just ci 160 passed.

title: espectacular hard gate: init config, author pilot contracts, wire pre-commit/CI
description:
Wire ah (espectacular) as a HARD gate over the openspec scenario corpus. Per Rule-of-5 review CORR-001 (TypeSafe-verified, 2026-10-03): wiring blocked TODAY is not because of missing contracts but because ah fails at config load (exit 1, '.espectacular/config.toml not found') — config init is the first blocker, contracts second, wiring last. 123 deployed Scenario blocks across 11 capability specs need contract TOMLs (decision note est. 2-4 days); pilot scope first.

Constraint (unchanged): espectacular is READ-ONLY over openspec/ — contracts live in .espectacular/, never edit specs from the tool. Requires specodelic-tlv landed first (guard must allow espectacular wiring).

TDD shape:

1. RED: run `ah check` after `ah init` — assert structural findings list missing contracts for the pilot specs (lint-findings: 2 scenarios, doctor: 7). The failing assertion: pilot-scope scenarios resolve to zero missing contracts.

2. GREEN: author contracts for the bounded pilot set (9 scenarios total) resolving against named tests. Test discovery: `ah report` produces the spec-to-contract matrix; find candidate named tests via `cargo test -- --list | grep -i <scenario-keyword>` (e.g. lint-findings scenarios -> lint findings tests; doctor scenarios -> tests covering doctor output). Then wire: structural `ah check` in lefthook.yml pre-commit inside the existing <!-- SPK:START --> marker block, and `ah check --run-tests` in a `guard-espectacular` recipe wired into `just ci` (EDGE-003: keep test execution out of pre-commit for commit latency).

3. REFACTOR: file a SEPARATE follow-up ticket to extend contracts from pilot set (9) to all 123 scenarios, staged per-capability. Do NOT absorb that scale-up here.

Acceptance (machine-checkable):
- Seeded contract violation (edit a contract to bind a failing/nonexistent test) makes the gate exit nonzero; restored contract passes.
- `ah check` exits 0 on HEAD for pilot scope; `just ci` includes guard-espectacular.

Must gate: gate exits nonzero on >=1 seeded contract violation; exits 0 on HEAD; 100% of pilot scenarios (9/9) have resolving contracts. Meter: `ah check --run-tests` (executes pilot contract tests).

Anti-goals: do NOT edit openspec/specs/ or openspec/changes/ to make scenarios pass (read-only constraint — espectacular must never drive spec edits); do NOT waive/skip scenarios to force green; do NOT bundle the 123-scenario scale-up here; do NOT run --run-tests in pre-commit.

Blocked by: specodelic-tlv (policy revision must land before wiring).

description:

title: mechanism: vocabulary-triggered orphan labeling (no pack, no uses edge)
description: Found by the add-bioimage-pack D6 pilot probes (2026-10-03). packs.md's orphan_vocabulary_labeled constraint: declared vocabulary used with no pack discovered or declared produces a labeled failure finding, prefix-derived when only the namespace is known. packs.rs implements only the declared-uses-edge half (src/packs.rs consumer pass, 'orphan (typed, via uses edges)'); vocabulary-triggered orphan — pack vocabulary used, no pack discovered, no uses edge — falls through silently (verified: ## Data + data.dataset used with the data.lineage pack absent produced no orphan finding). Sibling packs' probes only exercised the uses-edge half (aal task 3.2). Fix: in pack_pass, when a spec's vocabulary hits no discovered pack, emit the labeled orphan finding deriving the candidate pack by namespace prefix (data.* → data.lineage) with both remediations. Keep advisory-first: files using no pack vocabulary lint byte-identically.
close_reason: Decision of record: the vocabulary half of orphan_vocabulary_labeled ships as a structured-position-only scan (commit b3f563a, pushed). Signal = pack-qualified (dotted) tokens in kind cells (frontmatter kind, Constraint/Property kind cells) or table column headers whose namespace matches no discovered pack's namespace — a pack's namespace is its id's first segment, dotless ids name their namespace directly. Prose stays unscanned (dotted prose tokens like compile.extraction_failure are not vocabulary) so no_pack_no_change holds byte-identically. Finding names the prefix-derived candidate pack (data.dataset → data.*) and both remediations; a concrete uses-edge orphan for the same namespace wins without duplication. Note: kind-cell tokens outside every pack's namespace ALSO still fire the closed-set walkers (linter-schema_shape) — two labeled findings on one token is honest, mp1 row 7 may revisit consolidation. Files: src/packs.rs (namespace_of + vocab scan in pack_pass), src/lint.rs (RULE_TABLE semantics covers both halves), tests/cli.rs (3 new pack tests), specs/CHANGELOG.md #107, docs/src/commands.md. Gates: just ci, lint-specs 0, openspec --all --strict 19/19, graph 0 dangling.

title: compile/verify: executable predicate fragments (mp1 row 7 option C) — the only path to a reachable verified gate
description:
The verified gate is unreachable by construction today, and nothing tracks the path out.

Ground truth (Rule-of-5 review, grounded by execution 2026-10-02):
- Every Properties row compiles to `todo_predicate!` (src/compile.rs:300) — compiles, panics at execution; verify honestly reports properties_failed.
- Both model-check backends report `exploration_only` with `invariants_checked: []` (src/model_check.rs:336, :565) — `no_counterexample` is never produced, so verify's model gate (verify.rs:186: only no_counterexample verifies) always fails.
- End-to-end run: compile ok -> model-check outcome=exploration_only -> verify status=properties_failed, verified:[].
- This is deliberate honest failure (specodelic-len), NOT a bug. But specodelic-mp1 row 7's decided path to reachability — option C, user-supplied Rust predicate fragments as a format Revision — has no follow-up ticket (bd search: no matches).

SCOPE:
1. Spec-first: the predicate-fragment format Revision (how user Rust predicates are authored in Properties/Transition rows, compiled verbatim vs interpreted, security/totality guards).
2. compile: emit real predicate bodies when a row opts into the executable fragment.
3. model_check: execute constraint-kind predicates as stateright invariants so `no_counterexample` becomes producible.
4. verify: end-to-end `verified` reachable on a demo fixture.

ANTI-GOALS: no silent partial passes; exploration_only stays the honest outcome wherever a predicate is not executable; no weakening of both_gates_required.

Discovery of record: Rule-of-5 review of the validate/compile gap analysis; Jev-verified (0.92-0.98).
close_reason: Executable predicate fragments shipped (specodelic.md Revision 15, mp1 row 7 option C): **rust:** marker in Property predicate / invariant Constraint expr cells, fragment = verbatim Rust (no mini-language). compile: validate_fragments labeled (law/guard/non-invariant/multi-marker/empty/hygiene), assert! body emission, String generator values (GenVal retired), ModelIR.invariants + module manifest comment (staleness covers fragment edits). model_check: run_executable — dependency-free scratch-crate BFS, panic=violation (invariant_totality), engine native-bfs, no_counterexample producible (first clean verdict), minimal trace by construction. verify: end-to-end verified reachable (fragments_reach_verified CLI test). title: kinds: Revision — fix tautological reject guard + acknowledge optional frontmatter keys (Ro5 CORR-002/003)
description:
Rule-of-5 corpus review (2026-10-01) CORR-002 + CORR-003 (both MEDIUM): two spec bugs in kinds.md, fixed together under a new Revision heading per append_only_variants (rewordings narrow nothing).

CORR-002 — kinds.md:51 (reject transition guard) is a TAUTOLOGY. The guard is `¬(intent_row_shape ∧ constraint_row_shape ∧ state_row_shape ∧ transition_row_shape ∧ property_row_shape)`; no single row can satisfy all five mutually-exclusive shape conditions, so the conjunction is always false and reject fires unconditionally from shape_checked — well-formed rows have both accept and reject enabled (non-deterministic model). Fix: negate the applicable disjunct — `¬((row.kind==Intent ∧ [[kinds.intent_row_shape]]) ∨ (row.kind==Constraint ∧ [[kinds.constraint_row_shape]]) ∨ (row.kind==State ∧ ...) ∨ (row.kind==Transition ∧ ...) ∨ (row.kind==Property ∧ ...))`. Contrast (keep as-is): linter-graph_shape.md:40's same-shaped reject is correct — its four conjuncts co-apply to one artifact.

CORR-003 — kinds.md:24 intent_row_shape says frontmatter fields are "exactly {id, kind, statement}", but 10 corpus files carry a fourth key `checked_against_core` (documented in specs/AGENTS.md, undeclared in the format). constraint_row_shape received the optional-declared-columns carve-out in specodelic.md Revision 9; intent_row_shape never did. Fix: reword to {id, kind, statement} plus optionally-declared frontmatter keys (currently checked_against_core, per specs/AGENTS.md), mirroring the Rev 9 move. The linter's frontmatter_valid is a subset check so this is lint-blind — the spec text is the only guard.

SCOPE: new Revision heading in kinds.md (and a pointer note in specodelic.md's revision history only if kinds.md's discipline requires it — check kinds.md's own Revision conventions). TDD where the shape is testable: the reject-guard rewording is prose/expr-level; the testable slice is a fixture spec with an extra frontmatter key asserted accepted under the reworded intent_row_shape reading (and the linter's subset behavior documented, not changed). CHANGELOG entry.
acceptance_criteria: Must: (1) kinds.md reject guard reads the negation of the applicable disjunct (per-kind, not the tautological all-shapes conjunction); (2) intent_row_shape acknowledges optionally-declared frontmatter keys (checked_against_core) under a new Revision heading; (3) a fixture spec with an extra frontmatter key still lints clean. Meter: cargo test --test cli (fixture: extra-frontmatter-key spec accepted); just ci green; spk lint specs 0 issues. Anti-goals: no linter behavior change (frontmatter_valid stays a subset check — the spec text is the fix), no Reference Typing changes, no revision renumbering.
notes: Co-modification note (PRE-002): specs/specodelic.md and specs/CHANGELOG.md are also claimed by specodelic-5f2 — land sequentially (this ticket first: it establishes the Revision-heading precedent 5f2 cites), reconcile CHANGELOG numbering at merge.

description:

CLAR-001 — three mutually inconsistent checker-file counts. specs/specodelic.md:82 prose says "the join point of seven independently-specified checker files" while its own Checker Ownership table lists 8 gating rows (failure_shape was added 2026-09-30 without updating prose). specs/STATUS.md:386 (§1 reading order step 6) says "Read the six checker files" and omits linter-failure_shape.md from the order entirely; STATUS.md:202 quotes the stale "seven" claim. Actual: 8 gating checkers.

EDGE-001 — linter-observability.md and linter-external_completeness.md are checker files (spec-of-a-linter-check instances) but appear nowhere in the Checker Ownership table, with no stated reason at the table. A reader tracing the `linted` join cannot distinguish "deliberately excluded (advisory / never-gating)" from "forgotten". Fix: a one-line note under the table naming the two non-gating checker files, their severity channels (observability = warnings/exit 0; external_completeness = never gating per orchestrate.md), and why they sit outside the join.

CLAR-002 — specs/specodelic.md:143 links theory.md#document-instance-functor-copresheaf, but specs/theory.md:44's heading "Document instance (functor / copresheaf)" slugs with a double hyphen (" / " → "--") in GitHub/mdBook, so the anchor breaks in every rendered surface (including the deployed docs site). Fix: reword the heading to avoid " / " (e.g. "Document instance (functor and copresheaf)") and update the link at specodelic.md:143.

SCOPE: prose-only sweep, no schema change, no Revision heading required for pure count/prose corrections (verify against specodelic.md's append-only discipline — historical Revision sections are append-only, but the LIVE table/prose fixes are corrections of record; follow the Revision 3 precedent where a review's fixes landed under a new Revision heading). Update STATUS.md §1 (202 quote + step 6 reading order), specodelic.md:82, theory.md:44 + specodelic.md:143 link. Run doc-link-verifier or equivalent anchor check after. CHANGELOG entry.
acceptance_criteria: Must: (1) specodelic.md:82 says eight and matches the ownership table row count; (2) STATUS.md §1 step 6 includes linter-failure_shape.md in the reading order and the :202 quote no longer says seven; (3) the ownership table carries a one-line note naming linter-observability/external_completeness as non-gating and why; (4) theory.md copresheaf heading contains no '/' and the specodelic.md:143 link resolves against it. Meter: grep -c '^| .linter-' specs/specodelic.md == prose count; grep 'six checker' specs/STATUS.md finds nothing; anchor check: python3 scripts or mdbook-rendered grep of heading slug vs link; just lint-specs 0 issues (prose_untouched holds). Anti-goals: no schema/variant changes, no edits inside historical Revision sections (append-only), no CHANGELOG entry edits older than the new one.
notes: Co-modification note (PRE-002) + ordering (DEP-001): specs/specodelic.md and specs/CHANGELOG.md are also claimed by specodelic-x4w — land AFTER x4w (it sets the Revision-heading precedent this ticket's corrections follow); re-check specodelic.md line numbers and CHANGELOG numbering against the post-x4w tree before editing.

title: graph::build extracts edges from untyped link columns (violates graph.md total_extraction closed union)
description:
Found by the specodelic-vv8 conformance matrix (tests/conformance_matrix.rs, gap case total_refs_dangling).

specs/graph.md total_extraction pins the edge set to the CLOSED union traces_to/derives_from/guard/from/to/supersedes/emits/observes. graph::build (src/graph.rs) instead walks ALL links from spec.links and records an edge whenever typing_violation returns None — typing_violation's match falls through to None for untyped columns, so a link in an untyped column (e.g. a [[ref]] inside a predicate cell) becomes an edge and can dangle.

Repro: a clean corpus file with [[missing.file]] inside a properties.predicate cell — spk graph reports graph.dangling [clean -> [[missing.file]]] although predicate is not a reference field.

Fix direction: filter link columns to the closed union before edge extraction (dangling resolution for total_refs stays in the linter, which already scopes correctly).

Flip: tests/conformance_matrix.rs conformance_matrix_known_gaps case total_refs_dangling — move into cases(), drop the ignore.
close_reason:
Fixed in 514b153 (pushed). graph::build's links loop now skips every column outside the typed reference set {traces_to, derives_from, guard, supersedes, emits, satisfies, observes}: no edge, no graph dangling, no typing for untyped columns (expr/predicate/generator/frontmatter) — resolution of non-reference links stays total_refs' beat in the linter. from/to excluded from the links loop by design: the transitions walk owns those fields, so nothing double-records.

Deliberate deviation from the ticket's literal fix direction: the filter reads the Reference Typing TABLE's field set (the authority), not graph.md's parenthetical — satisfies joined the typed fields in Revision 7 and errors.md's contract_satisfied_from_consumer pins satisfies edges as extracted, so filtering it out would break a pinned property. graph.md's total_extraction enumeration reconciled to restate the table (CHANGELOG #77). The other two known-gaps cases (constraint_derives_cycle, orphan_property) stay #[ignore]d — their tickets (huf/rk3 territory) are unaffected.

Flip done: total_refs_dangling moved into cases() ungated. Corpus: 33 non-reference edges removed, dangling 0, violations 0, cycles 0. Gates: just ci, lint-specs 21/0, openspec strict, sync-sections, fuzz (300 lib/30 CLI iters) + differential legs re-run clean.

title: openspec change proposal: update-law-named-cases
description:

But WHERE cases appear in the predicate is free text; the linter cannot distinguish a real case from prose mentioning one.

Scope:

- Law predicates enumerate cases in machine-findable form (e.g. case "associativity": expr); linter verifies law_requires_cases cases present; extra named cases become checkable declarations

Workflow: fresh session, openspec scaffold proposal.md/tasks.md/deltas, openspec validate <id> --strict, approval gate before implementation.

title: Disambiguate terminology: project vs format vs tool vs subject
description:
Self-reference confusion in the corpus: 'specodelic' is used for the project, the format, and the tool interchangeably (STATUS.md:12 'markdown-based specification format' vs AGENTS.md:124 'a Rust CLI ... for the Specodelic specification format' vs specodelic.md:12 'written in the specodelic, about the specodelic').

Established via Rule-of-5 review of the three-layer proposal:
1. **the format** — the markdown schema/language (specodelic.md, kinds.md, theory.md)
2. **the tool (spk)** — the CLI whose behavior the linter-*.md / orchestrate.md corpus specifies
3. **the subject** — what a file specifies (for this corpus: the tool itself, i.e. dogfooding; elsewhere: anything). NOTE (CORR-002): subject is declared by a file's statement + prose, NOT a frontmatter field — and is un-lintable by design (prose_untouched).

Litmus test (subject-relative per CORR-001): an expr mentioning the checker/pipeline is layer conflation IFF the file's subject is not the tool. orchestrate.md mentioning checkers is legitimate — its subject IS the pipeline.

Also disambiguate 'spec' (4 senses: spec file / the format / the specs/ corpus / legacy spec-format, provenance-only per AGENTS.md rename note). Sanction adjectival compounds ('specodelic format'); bare 'specodelic' as noun for format/tool is the violation.

Scope is prose governance only (USAGE.md / AGENTS.md); no lint rule possible — prose_untouched.
design: Deliverable is un-lintable prose (prose_untouched), so make it self-testing: before/after sentence rewrites as acceptance criteria + grep sweep as the verification step. Keep it out of the four-layer shape entirely.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Terminology section added to specs/USAGE.md (or specs/AGENTS.md) with the three-layer table + 'spec' senses + usage before/after pairs.
2. Fixed sentence in specodelic.md line ~12: 'a spec written in the specodelic, about the specodelic' -> e.g. 'a spec written in the format, about the tool that checks it'.
3. STATUS.md §1 opening definition qualified (project vs format vs tool).
4. Grep sweep over specs/ + AGENTS.md for bare 'specodelic' used as noun for format/tool — each hit fixed or annotated as sanctioned.
5. No frontmatter schema change (explicitly decided against under append_only_variants).

The blocker no longer exists; the AGENTS.md text is stale and should be refreshed by governance, not by this ticket.

description:

title: Explore: contract-wiring checker — spec-level interface impedance from declared dataflow
description:
Exploration ticket (Rule-of-5 reviewed design conversation, 2026-09-29). Goal: decide whether a checker can detect interface absence and impedance at the SPEC level, using only declared/typed wiring — no source analysis.

Detectable structural patterns (from spk graph edges):
1. Published-unconsumed: extension_point Constraint with zero inbound satisfies edges.
2. Consumed-unpublished: satisfies pointing at nonexistent/unpublished contract (dangling or typing violation today — check if the message is interface-shaped enough).
3. Emitted-unobserved: emits→effect with zero observes — NOTE: add-observability-contracts landed 2026-09-30; linter.observability already enforces this advisory rule corpus-wide. This ticket must NOT duplicate it — only assess whether cross-file observability gaps need a graph-level view beyond the lint rule.
4. Unlinked expectation: a consumer-side constraint describing a contract's shape with NO derives_from edge to the producer's published contract constraint — the spec-level analog of an untyped interface. Weakest but most novel signal.

Hard precondition: all patterns require corpora to declare wiring in structured cells; prose wiring is invisible (evidence: bajan's extraction.claims→eval.claims wiring lives in prose only — CORR-001). Impedance proper (shape divergence) is only comparable where BOTH sides model contract shape as structured rows.

Deliverable: decision note (feasible / not / partial + which patterns) — no implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Spike notes exist answering (a)(b)(c); each candidate pattern has a defined fixture/test shape or is rejected with evidence; decision recorded whether to proceed to a change proposal; no production code changes in this ticket
notes: REVIEW FIXES (issue-review, converged pass 5): (1) Spike-notes destination: commit as openspec/research/contract-wiring-spike.md (house precedent: specodelic-4ae decision note under openspec/). (2) Meter (run verbatim at base_commit): cargo run -q -- graph -j specs | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d['data']['graph']['violations']))" — expect 38; per-pattern fixture corpora live in tests/cli.rs fixtures once a proposal lands. (3) Decision point is HITL: maintainer decides go/no-go; spike output is the input. (4) metadata.files are PROSPECTIVE files the outcome would reshape (spike itself touches none).

title: [feature] spk migrate: wrap an existing openspec delta in the four-layer dual-format skeleton (gh#6 item 4)
description:
From gh issue charly-vibes/specodelic#6 item 1 (highest-value per adopter who migrated 25 deltas by hand). The dual-format migration recipe (frontmatter + derive tables + byte-identical ## Requirements mirror) is fully manual; the mirror invites sed one-liners.

Proposal shape (from the issue): spk migrate <spec.md> wraps an existing delta in place — read ## ADDED Requirements, generate frontmatter (id: spec per naming law, EARS statement stub) + empty Constraints/Model/Properties layers + byte-identical ## Requirements mirror; never destroys the delta text. title: [bug/gh#4] explain dual-format overpromises: section-sync not enforced by spk lint; footer hint cites nonexistent Notes field
description:
From gh issue charly-vibes/specodelic#4 (adopter, spk 0.1.0; verified on main 2026-09-29).

1. {"ok":true,"envelope_version":"0.1","cli_version":"0.1.0","envelope_kind":"ok","data":{"body":"# dual-format

Where specodelic meets **OpenSpec**: this repo manages its engineering
change workflow in openspec (proposals → tasks → archive), and every
change delta is also a lint-clean specodelic file. One markdown file,
two parsers, requirement text authored once.

A **dual-format file** carries both grammars:

- Specodelic half: YAML frontmatter (`id: spec`, `kind: intent`, an
  EARS `statement`) plus the `## Constraints`, `## Model`, and
  `## Properties` tables.
- Openspec half: `## Purpose`, `## ADDED Requirements`, and a sibling
  `## Requirements` section with identical text.

**Naming law**: openspec hard-requires the delta filename `spec.md`,
so dual-format files declare `id: spec` (the `-` ⇔ `.` mapping makes
that the legal id). Uniqueness is per-file — any number of `id: spec`
files coexist. Deltas stay self-contained: `[[wiki-refs]]` resolve
only within the file; domain semantics are cited by prose path
(`specs/<name>.md`), never wiki-link.

**Enforcement**: `linter.dual_format_valid` — a file carrying
`## ADDED Requirements` must declare `id: spec` and pair it with the
sibling `## Requirements` section; a capability spec under
`openspec/specs/` must be dual-format or CI fails. The section-sync
check fails on drift between the two requirement sections.

**Migration** (plain openspec file → compliant):

1. Add the frontmatter: `id: spec`, `kind: intent`, one EARS `SHALL`
   statement condensing the requirements.
2. Derive the tables: one `invariant` Constraint per MUST the
   requirements imply, a Model covering the scenarios, one unit
   Property deriving from each constraint (the coverage rule).
3. Mirror `## Requirements` (identical text to `## ADDED
   Requirements`); a plain capability spec keeps only
   `## Requirements`.
4. Gates: `spk lint <file>`, `openspec validate --all --strict`, and
   the section-sync check must all pass.","format_revision":"specodelic.md Revision 8","topic":"dual-format"},"warnings":[],"hints":[{"command":"→ Run: apply the format, then check with: specodelic lint","description":"apply the format, then check with: specodelic lint
  → Run: apply the format, then check with: specodelic lint"}],"meta":{"duration_ms":0,"tx":null,"request_id":null}} says 'The section-sync check fails on drift between the two requirement sections' — but that check lives in THIS repo's scripts/check_section_sync.py (just ci), not in the spk binary. Drifted-mirror fixture lints clean (verified). FIX (this ticket): implement requirement-section drift detection in the linter — a file carrying both ## ADDED Requirements and ## Requirements must have identical section text; new finding in the dual_format_valid family (extend the rule or add requirement_drift), RULE_TABLE entry, tests, spec/docs sync.
2. lint failure footer hint (src/main.rs:913) says 'cite the governing constraint in Notes if it's a false positive' — no Notes field exists anywhere in the format. Reword to point at what exists (spk explain lint-rules).
3. explain dual-format should state where section-sync currently lives (repo recipe) until lint enforces it, and that orchestrate is a stub.

TDD: drifted-mirror fixture -> finding (red), identical mirror -> clean; footer text test.

title: [feature/gh#2.1] bare row refs in id:spec dual-format files: resolve against own rows (or document the file-qualification requirement with an example)
description:
From gh issue charly-vibes/specodelic#2 point 1. RE-SCOPED after issue-review 2026-09-29: the 'document the file-qualification requirement' leg is DONE (specodelic-ar2/gh#3 + specodelic-vi2: explain references/dual-format + scaffold + self-file hint). REMAINING SCOPE — the enforcement decision only:

Option A: bare row refs in id:spec files resolve against their OWN rows (compat: bare [[c]] currently is metasyntactic-skipped by is_metasyntactic — dotless unknown targets vanish silently; lint.rs total_refs + graph.rs resolve() must both change, plus the coverage rule's bare-id arm derived.contains(*cid) already accepts the bare form).
Option B: keep file-qualification mandatory but make the metasyntactic skip stop eating dotted-less row refs silently (emit a labeled finding instead of silence).

MUST: an id:spec fixture with [[row-id]] behaves per the chosen option in BOTH lint and graph; decision recorded as a comment on this ticket before implementation (HITL: affects every existing dual-format author). Corpus behavior must not change for file-qualified refs.
METER: cargo test; spk lint + graph on a synthetic dual-format fixture pair.
ANTI-GOALS: no change to cross-file resolution for non-dual ids; no new spec revision required if Option B.
FILES: src/lint.rs, src/graph.rs. File-header required.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Empirical finding from the specodelic-ar2 Ro5 review (2026-09-29): the file-qualification law documented for gh#3 is NOT what the checkers enforce. Fixture: id:spec file with guard [[c]] and derives_from [[c]] (bare, dotless) — spk lint = 0 issues (metasyntactic skip), coverage's bare-id arm (lint.rs derived.contains(*cid)) COUNTS it as covering, spk graph = 0 dangling but 0 edges (silent vanish). Bare TEXT (no brackets) is the only loudly-failing form (no_orphan_property). So the 'document the file-qualification requirement' leg of this ticket is done (guide/gh#3), but the checker-side work remains: either enforce the law (reject bare row refs in id:spec files / make bare refs resolve against own rows = this ticket's original ask) or align coverage's bare-id acceptance with the documented law. Also relevant: is_metasyntactic's dotless skip is what eats the refs — any enforcement change must decide what happens to the scaffold's old '[[id]]' pattern consumers may have copied.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Decision of record (user-approved 2026-09-29): Option A — bare row refs in id:spec files resolve against the file's OWN rows, in both lint and graph. Rationale: the self-containment law (#42) already scopes id:spec resolution file-locally, so a dotless target naming an own row has exactly one possible meaning; and the coverage rule already accepted the bare form, so Option B would have left two rules contradicting each other. Scope: dotless targets only (dotful keep the gh#5 hint — genuinely ambiguous with file.row); unknown bare targets keep the metasyntactic skip; typing violations on bare refs become visible. Implemented TDD: 4 tests; corpus churn zero.

title: [feature/gh#2.2] corpus discovery: bare spk lint finds nothing in consumer repos — configured corpus path or a discovery hint
description:
From gh issue charly-vibes/specodelic#2 point 2. Options (pick at design time): (a) honor a configured corpus path — env var (e.g. SPECODELIC_CORPUS) and/or a line in the SPECODELIC managed block that spk init writes, so bare spk lint works after init; (b) minimal: when lint/graph find zero files and an openspec/ tree exists, the failure hint should say 'found an openspec/ tree — try: spk lint openspec'; (c) doctor gains a corpus-discovery check that names the discovery rule ('pass a directory containing *.md specs; hidden and build dirs are skipped').

Note the interplay with the new exit-code contract (specodelic-7rr): bare spk lint finding nothing is an invocation error (exit 2) — the hint rides that failure envelope, so option (b)/(c) compose with it cleanly.

comments.author: charly vibes

comments.text: Decision of record (design time): option (b)+(c). lint/graph zero-files failures name the openspec/ tree when present (composing with the 7rr exit-2 contract), and doctor gains a corpus-discovery check naming the discovery rule. Option (a) — configured corpus path (env var / managed-block line) — deliberately deferred: (b)+(c) fix the discoverability gap without new config surface; revisit only if adopters report the hint is insufficient.

title: Tighten output contract: error envelopes carry ok:true, exit-code ambiguity, --human is Rust Debug output, '→ Run: run:' hint duplication
description:
All four reproduced 2026-09-28:

1. ok:true on errors — root cause is upstream genesis-vibes 0.8.1: Output::to_envelope (guide.rs:486) unconditionally calls Envelope::success() even when is_error=true, so JSON reads {"ok":true,"envelope_kind":"error"}. Envelope::error() exists but is never used. Fix in genesis (to_envelope must honor is_error), then specodelic picks it up on the next genesis bump. Genesis repo ticket if there is one; keep a local regression test asserting error envelopes serialize ok:false.
2. Exit code 1 covers both 'lint findings' and 'path not found' — consumers cannot distinguish 'your spec is bad' from 'you typoed the path'. Give not-found/no-files a distinct code (or an explicit machine-readable cause) and document the mapping.
3. --human output is literally Rust {:?} Debug of serde_json::Value (Object { … String(…) }) — render lint/graph/model-check reports as real human text (per-report formatters), keep Debug only for internal logs.
4. Hint rendering duplicates: hints authored as 'run: specodelic graph' emit '→ Run: run: specodelic graph' (genesis Suggestion::fix footer + message()). Either strip a leading 'run: ' at render time or fix authoring convention; also the hint command+description fields duplicate the same text.

RED→GREEN per item; REGRESSION: cargo test suites + snapshot tests for --human output.
Evidence: review round 2, issues 4-5.
notes: CLARITY 2026-09-29: exit-code mapping pinned — 0 = success (lint with zero findings counts); 1 = stage produced findings/tool-level failure (current behavior); 2 = invocation error (path not found, no files matched, unreadable input). Document the mapping in README/USAGE and in --help after_help; consumers distinguish via exit code, and the JSON envelope's envelope_kind must agree. title: Implement specodelic rename: atomic id rename with link rewrite

title: Implement specodelic verify: execute proptest blocks + gate
description:
Per specs/verify.md. Run every proptest! block compile produced to completion; transition a file to verified only when all pass AND model_check's most recent run against the CURRENT compiled artifact is clean.

MUST: a file with a failing proptest block is NOT verified; a file whose model_check result is stale (artifact changed since the run) is NOT verified; only the conjunction verifies.
METER: `spk verify <file> --json` → .data.status == "verified" exactly in that case, else the blocking stage is named.

title: decide: fan-in multiplicity rule — state_view counts (source,field) pairs, traceability_view counts distinct sources (B3)
description:
Split out of specodelic-ils (issue-review SCOPE-001). From the 2026-10-08 GLM report, finding B3; verified at bd6585b.

**The disagreement**: scripts/state_view.py:119 counts fan-in over DISTINCT `(source, field)` pairs; scripts/traceability_view.py:114 counts DISTINCT source intents — both cite "D2's multiplicity rule". state_view.py:16's own header says "fan-in counts DISTINCT sources", contradicting its implementation at :119.

**Impact**: the same corpus renders different fan-in labels in two views; one source with both a transitions.from and a transitions.guard edge into the same target counts twice in the state view but once in traceability.

**Design-lane work**: choose the canonical rule, update design D2 if the (source, field) refinement is intentional, then make both views share one implementation.
design: Pick one rule (design D2 of add-graph-views says distinct sources), make both views share one implementation (view_common.fan_in call sites), and fix state_view.py:16's header to match.

Meter: a two-edge fixture (one source with transitions.from + transitions.guard into the same target) renders identical fan-in counts in state and traceability views; python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts passes.

title: decide: kernel-grammar gate placement (lint vs compile) + derive TYPED_REFERENCE_COLUMNS from schema (F5 + Grok risk)
description:
Two related design decisions surfaced by the 2026-10-08 evaluations; behavior re-verified at bd6585b.

**F5 — lint accepts kernel cells that compile rejects.** All of these exit 0 from `spk lint` and exit 1 from `spk compile`: empty `**kernel:**` marker, unclosed parenthesis, `∨` (only `∧`/`¬` exist), `acyclic(traces_to)` (non-endo morphism), `resolves(nonexistent_col)`, `forall c in Constraint: …`.

Why it matters: AGENTS.md tells contributors to gate on lint; a lint-only gate lets malformed kernel cells through to compile time. UNKNOWN whether lint is *meant* to stay grammar-agnostic — grep of specs/linter-*.md finds no kernel rows; specs/compile.md places grammar failures at the compile extraction stage. So possibly by design.

**Decision needed**: either (a) add kernel-grammar validation to lint (new linter rule, red→green in specs/linter-*.md first), or (b) document that compile is the grammar gate and adjust contributor guidance.

**TYPED_REFERENCE_COLUMNS — hard-coded constant.** src/graph.rs:179: `pub(crate) const TYPED_REFERENCE_COLUMNS: [&str; 7]`. If the acset Schema gains a typed column without updating the constant, the graph silently omits those edges (Grok report's medium process risk). Fix: derive the extraction list from the schema value, or add a test asserting the constant matches the Schema export under the same gate as the typing table.

See also specodelic-xci (tautology/placeholder advisories) — related lint-hardening space.
acceptance_criteria: Must: a recorded decision for (1) kernel-grammar gate placement (lint rule with red-first test, or documented compile-as-gate + contributor-guidance edit) and (2) deriving TYPED_REFERENCE_COLUMNS from the acset Schema (or a gate test asserting constant==Schema). Meter: decision record exists in openspec/decisions/; grep -n TYPED_REFERENCE_COLUMNS src/graph.rs shows derivation or an adjacent assertion test; just ci green.

title: view scripts: type-based hint routing, Mermaid label escaping, kernel_grammar docstring (B1/B2/B4)
description:
Batch of small findings from the 2026-10-08 GLM report; all re-verified at bd6585b.

**B1 — hint routed by substring.** scripts/graph_views.py:140: `hint = LINT_HINT if "lint" in str(error) else …`. An `ArtifactInvalid` raised while parsing the lint *envelope itself* ("lint envelope carries no issues list", view_common.py) contains "lint" and gets the fix-your-invariants hint. Use the exception type (already computed one line above as `refused`/`failure`) as the discriminator.

**B2 — incomplete Mermaid escaping.** scripts/view_common.py:184 `mermaid_escape` only replaces `"`. Labels embed arbitrary spec-cell text; `-->`, `#`, `%%`, or a line starting `end` can break or alter the rendered diagram. Views are generated in CI and published — mild injection surface. Undermines design D8 (deterministic text output). Mirror the fix into src/graph.rs's `mermaid_escape` if it shares the gap.

**B3 — fan-in definitions disagree.** scripts/state_view.py:119 counts fan-in over DISTINCT `(source, field)` pairs; scripts/traceability_view.py:114 counts DISTINCT source intents — both cite "D2's multiplicity rule". Worse, state_view.py:16's own header says "fan-in counts DISTINCT sources", contradicting its implementation at :119. Pick one rule (design D2 says distinct sources), fix state_view, cite it consistently.

**B4 — docstring contradicts spec and tests.** tests/kernel_grammar.rs:5 claims "marker-free whole-cell opt-in"; the spec (`kernel_expr_opt_in`, specs/compile.md) and the tests themselves require a `**kernel:**` marker. Comment-only fix.

**B5 — changelog naming (closed).** src/compile.rs:537-538 emits the openspec change names; CHANGELOG #114's beads-id strings are the stale side. Fold into specodelic-s64 (docs readiness) if preferred — closing this item is fine either way, the others are code.
acceptance_criteria: Must (post-split scope B1+B2+B4): hint routing discriminates on exception type; mermaid_escape neutralizes -->, #, %%, and line-leading end; kernel_grammar.rs docstring says marker-based opt-in. Meter: new unit tests for the escape cases and hint routing pass under python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts; grep -c 'marker-free whole-cell opt-in' tests/kernel_grammar.rs = 0.
notes: SCOPE CHANGE (post-review): B5 (changelog hint naming) moved to specodelic-s64 — do NOT edit specs/CHANGELOG.md in this ticket. B3 (fan-in rule disagreement) moved to its own design ticket. This ticket now covers B1+B2+B4 only.

title: model-check: claim records omit reason when not verified — dangling reachable yields unlabeled unknown (F4/F6)
description:
From the 2026-10-08 Claude report (F4, F6); re-verified at bd6585b.

**Observed**: a kernel claim with status `unknown` persists exactly `{"evaluator":"kernel","id":"refund_traces_resolve","status":"unknown"}` — no reason. Human output reads `blocking: refund_traces_resolve (kernel, unknown)` with no explanation. Repro: `reachable(order.cancel.nope, order.cancel.refund_bounded, guard)` — a dangling endpoint lints and compiles, then evaluates to `unknown`, downgrading the run to `exploration_only` with nothing pointing at the bad id.

**Expected**: specs/model_check.md:35 (`claim_report_schema`) — records carry "id, evaluator kind, status, reason where not verified"; :76 (`unknown_or_missing_claim_blocks_clean`) — reasons name the claim ids.

**Cause**: src/kernel.rs native evaluation returns `ThreeValued::Unknown` with `reason: None` for evaluation errors (~872-892, 1090-1115); reasons attach only on the TLC path and the re-parse-failure fallback.

**Diagnosability asymmetry**: a mistyped morphism in `resolves(...)` gets a labeled compile error; a mistyped endpoint in `reachable(...)` gets unlabeled `unknown`. The unknown itself is deliberate ("never a fabricated verdict") — the fix is attaching the reason, not changing the verdict.

**Also verify while here** (UNKNOWN from the report): whether `counterexample` records carry `reason`.
acceptance_criteria: Must: kernel-claim records with status unknown or counterexample carry a non-empty reason naming the failure, per specs/model_check.md claim_report_schema; counterexample-record reason presence verified either way in a test. Meter: the appended repro — the persisted specodelic/*.check.json record for refund_traces_resolve has a non-empty reason field; absent reason = not done.
notes:
REPRO:
spk compile order-cancel.md   # quick-start spec from specs/USAGE.md §1
sed -i 's/resolves(traces_to)/reachable(order.cancel.nope, order.cancel.refund_bounded, guard)/' order-cancel.md
spk model-check order-cancel.md   # exit 0, outcome exploration_only
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('specodelic/order-cancel.check.json'));print(d['claims'])"
# -> {'evaluator': 'kernel', 'id': 'refund_traces_resolve', 'status': 'unknown'} — no reason

title: graph: projection exit-code semantics — bad path silent success, violations exit 0 in text modes (F3+F8)
description:
From the 2026-10-08 Claude report (F3, F8); both re-verified at bd6585b.

**F3**: `spk graph /nonexistent --format edges` → exit 0, empty stdout/stderr. JSON mode exits 2. A typo'd path looks like an empty corpus. `--help` says "Zero spec files exit 0 with empty output" but a nonexistent path is not zero spec files; no spec text sanctions silent success on an unreadable path.

**F8**: `spk graph tests/fixtures/typing_violations` → JSON exits 1; same fixture with `--format edges` → **exit 0** (violations ride along as annotation rows per design D3, which is correct — but the exit code is unspecified, so a pipeline cannot gate on violations).

**Fix direction**: one decision covering projection modes —
- unreadable/nonexistent path → exit 2 (labeled, matching JSON mode and `spk lint` behavior);
- typing violations present in text projections → exit 1 (matching JSON mode), violations still riding along in output.

Repro:
```
spk graph /nonexistent --format edges; echo $?          # 0, should be 2
spk graph tests/fixtures/typing_violations --format edges >/dev/null; echo $?  # 0, should be 1
```
acceptance_criteria: Must: a nonexistent/unreadable path in projection modes exits 2 with a labeled error; typing violations in text projections exit 1 while violations still ride along as annotation rows. Meter: the body's two repro lines print 2 and 1 respectively; graph --format edges on tests/fixtures/typing_violations still emits the six annotation rows.
notes:
ANTI-GOALS: do not silently drop violations from projection output to make exit codes align; violations must still ride along (design D3); do not change JSON-mode exit codes.
Implemented at 5b2f5fe: cmd_graph_projection (src/main.rs) exits 2 with a labeled refusal envelope on stderr for unresolved named roots (F3) and exits 1 when typing violations ride along in text projections (F8); annotation rows unchanged (D3). New tests/cli/graph_projection.rs; 4 stale exit-0 pins updated. Gates green: just test, clippy -D warnings, fmt, pretender check (vendored mermaid aside), just lint-specs, openspec validate, ah check. Note: just test needs vendor/mermaid.min.js moved aside until the vendor-threshold pretender.toml diff lands.

title: Graph views demonstrate faithful output on real corpora
description:
## Parent

specodelic-gre
Ref: openspec/changes/add-graph-views/proposal.md; design.md and tasks.md alongside.
Task references: add-graph-views:4.1; add-graph-views:4.2; add-graph-views:4.3; add-graph-views:4.4.
Source: .wai/resources/research/2026-10-06-ro5-proposal-review.md (resolved findings).

## What to build

Exercise this repo and read-only sibling bajan corpus, record real wiring/violation behavior, verify existing bajan-ac8 rather than filing a duplicate, then complete graph proposal gates.

Lane: REVIEW; complexity: L. Semantics are pinned in the reviewed proposal; if a new unresolved semantic choice appears, retag DESIGN rather than guessing.

**Files / Systems:**
- `openspec/changes/add-graph-views/tasks.md`
- `docs/src/graph-views.md` (proposed new path)
- `scripts/graph_views.py` (proposed new path)

## Verifiable Value Claim

**Must (hard gate):** Local clean corpus has 0 violation annotations and dirty fixture retains all violations
**Meter:** `just ci && openspec validate add-graph-views --strict` (run after adding the specified fixtures; zero selected tests does not pass).
**Baseline:** Not measured for this slice; capture the failing input/output in RED. Proposal validation is not runtime evidence.
**Regression suite:** `just ci`; preserve existing assertions, fixture meaning, and accepted legacy behavior except the explicitly documented proposal changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Local clean corpus has 0 violation annotations and dirty fixture retains all violations
- [ ] Sibling run uses 0 corpus-specific code edits
- [ ] Existing bajan-ac8 status is recorded without opening/closing sibling tickets
- [ ] All required gates pass and task completion is evidence-backed
- [ ] The RED test actually runs and fails for the intended reason before GREEN; record commands and results. A zero-test filtered run is not evidence.
- [ ] New source files have Purpose / Responsibilities / Rationale headers; contract-changing edits update Rationale.
- [ ] Bind new deployed scenarios to genuine tests as each slice lands; do not invent bindings or postpone required contracts until closure.
- [ ] Update only the corresponding OpenSpec task checkboxes after completion; preserve unrelated and closed work.

## Blocked by

specodelic-gre.9

## TDD and Tidy First

CRITICAL: Follow Test Driven Development and Tidy First throughout. Write
and observe the failing behavioral test first, then the smallest passing
implementation. For a cleanup-only ticket, establish green characterization
fixtures first and keep them unchanged. Any preparatory tidy and subsequent
refactoring use separate tickets and commits from feature behavior; use the
mapped TIDY issues, never bundle a new semantic change into cleanup.

## Anti-goals

- Do not weaken, delete, skip or rewrite expected results merely to pass the
  gate; intentional contract changes require the exact proposal scenario.
- Do not add dependencies, modify lockfiles or broaden public APIs beyond
  this slice's reviewed design. Declared pytest/Hypothesis or Vitest/fast-check
  test environments are allowed where required; never auto-install at runtime.
- Do not interpret prose as executable claims, fabricate evidence, implement
  guards, or build a new runner registry. Keep sibling-tool boundaries.
- Do not modify hooks ownership, reopen closed kernel history, or touch
  sibling repositories. Read-only sibling validation is allowed when scoped.
- No push, deployment or release authorization is conferred by this ticket.
  Archive only through the sanctioned dual-format recipe after all gates.

title: gate: seeded-violation drills must run in an isolated worktree or hold a concurrency lock
description: Remediation (a) of specodelic-dz4 (incident e7bb19e): a concurrent session committed a drill's in-flight seeded-violation state into the main working tree because drills run in-tree with no isolation. Scope: gate drills (ah check seeded-violation runs, guard-espectacular poison files) must either (1) run in a dedicated git worktree, or (2) hold an advisory lock (e.g. .beads/ or .genesis lock file) that a concurrent session's pre-commit checks before sweeping files. Prefer the mechanism that needs no new hook claims — note AGENTS.md: pretender owns core.hooksPath; any hook-side check must chain to .beads/hooks, never replace. Meter (quantified): drill refuses to run in-tree without lock/worktree (exit 2 with remediation hint), and a two-session rehearsal shows no cross-session commit of drill state; just ci green.
notes:
2026-10-05 (dz4 remediation-b decision): this ticket now OWNS the hook-side half of the interlock — the drill-lock check must live in scripts/guards/ wired via lefthook.yml pre-commit+pre-push and mirrored in just ci; do NOT edit .beads/hooks shims or claim core.hooksPath. Guard must print remediation hint + exit nonzero; handle stale/crash-orphaned locks without wedging commits. See openspec/decisions/2026-10-05-precommit-sweep-policy.md.
Meter met 2026-10-05: (1) gate-drill.sh refuses in-tree runs when a live lock is held (exit 2 + worktree hint); (2) two-session rehearsal on the real hook chain — drill held .beads/gate-drill.lock via gate-drill.sh, a concurrent git commit of a staged file was REFUSED (hook exit 1, full remediation hint), no drill state committed; lock auto-released on drill exit; (3) just ci green (160 passed). Caveat: lefthook skips the entire pre-commit for EMPTY commits (no staged files) — not an incident vector (nothing to sweep). 12 tests in tests/gate_drill_lock.rs.

- EDGE-002 (HIGH, conf 0.87): gluing is unspecified for None (dangling) entries. Specify: None glues with None per morphism and reports in the dangling report; a defined-target collision with None is NOT a conflict.

Also ships: the theory-fixed-schema-instances.patch (deferred from add-acset-core) and names the merge-compute CLI surface (CLAR-001).

description:
Per the contract-wiring spike (specodelic-x30, openspec/research/2026-10-01-contract-wiring-spike/decision.md — CORR-002 review pass endorsed exactly this follow-up and no other).

PROBLEM: when a typed consumption reference (satisfies, and by symmetry observes) fails to resolve, the graph reports the GENERIC dangling message:

  consumer → [[producer.nope]]

No interface framing. A reader cannot tell "typo'd row id" from "consuming a contract nobody published" — the remediation differs (fix the id vs publish the row). The wrong-kind case is ALREADY interface-shaped (typing violation: "satisfies must resolve to an extension_point Constraint (Reference Typing); target is a Constraint (kind `invariant`)") — do not touch that path.

SCOPE (message polish only — rides the existing dangling machinery in src/graph.rs, no new pattern):
- When link.column is a consumption column (satisfies, observes), render the dangling entry interface-shaped, e.g.:
  `consumer.hooks_installed (satisfies) → [[producer.nope]]: no published contract row `producer.nope` exists — publish it in the producer's file or fix the id`
- Keep non-consumption dangling messages unchanged (traces_to, derives_from, guard, transitions.* keep today's shape — other tooling/tests may pin them).
- Honesty rule: the message must NOT claim to know which remediation applies; it names both.

TDD SHAPE (RED-first): fixture corpus in tests/cli.rs (spike p2a shape — producer with one extension_point row, consumer effect row satisfying [[producer.nope]]): assert the dangling entry carries the consumption-column name and the interface-shaped hint. Add the observes-symmetry case (effect row observing [[ghost.row]]). Existing dangling tests must stay green (message-shape change is consumption-column-scoped).

SPEC CHECK: specs/graph.md and specs/linter-graph_shape.md do not pin the dangling message format today — verify; if a row pins message shape, update the spec row in the same commit (spec-first if so). The spike's p2a fixture shape is the derivation.

OUT OF SCOPE: any new checker/pattern (spike rejected all four as checkers); message changes for resolved-edge paths; changes to Violation (typing) messages.

SOURCE: specodelic-x30 spike evidence; user go-ahead 2026-10-01 (option a of {message-shape ticket / add-graph-views / P3 llms.txt}).

title: acyclic's edge set narrows derives_from to properties — spec invariant is unqualified
description:
Found by the specodelic-vv8 conformance matrix (tests/conformance_matrix.rs, gap case constraint_derives_cycle).

linter-graph_shape.md acyclic invariant: 'the directed graph formed by traces_to UNION derives_from UNION guard-as-edge has no cycle' — unqualified. The implementation (src/lint.rs, lint_graph_shape) builds the acyclic edge set from (constraints,traces_to), (properties,derives_from), (transitions,guard) ONLY — a CONSTRAINT-row derives_from edge is invisible.

A constraint<->constraint derives_from cycle is typing-legal (the Reference Typing table allows derives_from -> Constraint from any row), so it escapes BOTH the acyclic check and edge_kind_matches_typing — only single_root_reachable notices the island.

RESOLUTION MAY BE A SPEC DECISION, not a pure bug: constraint-level derives_from may be out-of-format (a constraint is derived FROM by properties, it does not derive). Options: (a) add (constraints,derives_from) to the acyclic edge set; (b) declare constraint-level derives_from invalid and enforce that instead (schema/lint rule); (c) amend linter-graph_shape.md's invariant to scope derives_from to properties. Pick one and flip the matrix case accordingly.

Flip: tests/conformance_matrix.rs conformance_matrix_known_gaps case constraint_derives_cycle — move into cases() (with whatever expectation the decision yields), drop the ignore.

title: no_orphan_property checks derives_from presence only — linter-coverage.md requires it to resolve to a real constraint
description:
Found by the specodelic-vv8 conformance matrix (tests/conformance_matrix.rs, gap case orphan_property).

linter-coverage.md no_orphan_property invariant: 'p.derives_from resolves to a real constraint'. The implementation (src/lint.rs, lint_coverage) checks only that A derives_from link exists on the property — not that its target resolves to a constraint row. A property deriving from a non-law PROPERTY passes the linter silently; only the graph layer's edge_kind_matches_typing flags it (derives_from must resolve to a Constraint unless the source is a law).

Two-layer defense exists, but the coverage checker's own invariant is not enforced by the checker that owns it.

Fix direction: resolve each derives_from target; if it resolves to a Property row and the source property is not law-kind, fire no_orphan_property. Unresolved targets stay total_refs' beat (the invariant restates total_refs, scoped to this edge).

Flip: tests/conformance_matrix.rs conformance_matrix_known_gaps case orphan_property — move into cases(), drop the ignore.

title: Implement specodelic refactor: tidy-first split advisor
description:
Per specs/refactor.md. Flag nodes with high, unrelated fan-in in the reference graph as tidy-first split candidates. Always non-gating (kind == effect, already excluded from every guard by the format's typing — no new "never gates" invariant needed).

MUST: a synthetic node with high unrelated fan-in is flagged; a node with coherent fan-in is not; output is advisory only (exit 0 either way).
METER: `spk refactor specs --json` on a synthetic fixture; cargo test.
ANTI-GOALS: never gate a pipeline stage on this advisory; don't invent a new invariant where the typing table already excludes effect constraints from guards.
HITL: whether "unrelated" keys off id namespace or directory placement — see specodelic-mp1 (flat namespace convention would make the advisory fire on almost everything).
FILES: src/refactor.rs; reuse graph.rs. File-header required.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Implemented (TDD, red→green): src/refactor.rs — advisor consumes GraphReport's derived edges only (fan_in_read_from_graph; never walks markdown). Finding shape = exactly {node_id, dependent_count, unrelated_namespace_count, suggested_split} per advisory_finding_emitted. Unrelated = NCA==root (row 3 decision of record). --high-fan-in = threshold_is_per_repo_setting (default 3, DEFAULT_HIGH_FAN_IN const). --changeset enables narrow_diff_heuristic: strict-subset touch + no dependency edges from changeset rows to the node's other owned rows → flag regardless of fan-in. Gotcha (fixture-shaping): traces_to→Constraint is typing-forbidden and the graph never records it — legal cross-row dependency edges only exist as Property derives_from→Constraint and guard→invariant Constraint, so dependent fixtures cite intents (traces_to) or properties (derives_from). 5 integration tests + unit-level const. Dogfood: corpus flags specodelic itself as top split candidate (12 unrelated dependents) — STATUS §2's named pathology, honestly advisory. just ci green; lint 0 issues; exit 0 either way (never gates).
